falsifiable_hypothesis: A duplicated callback is harmless and cannot double-count a unit or a metric row.
required_deliverable: Idempotence tests asserting repeated ingestion of an identical result produces exactly one registry effect and one metric row.

fault_classes.observed_behaviour: the first callback was ingested and the next four were suppressed; exactly one ingestion file, one result file, one registry INGESTION row and one PARENT_INGESTED event; verify_chain clean

the transaction identity (task, idempotency key, lease, fence, attempt, result commit, artifact hashes) was unchanged while the document bytes differed; the second callback was not suppressed and produced two ingestion files, two result files, two registry INGESTION rows and two PARENT_INGESTED events for one transaction
fault_classes.realism: workstreams/po03/tools/emit_result.py sets readback_verified_at and committed_at from utc_now() on every run, which was verified in its source, so any producer that re-emits after a lost callback sends exactly this shape

fault_classes.observed_behaviour: one ingestion suspended between its duplicate check and its first durable write while a second ingestion of the same document completed; the destination file stayed single, but the registry received two INGESTION rows and the event chain received two PARENT_INGESTED events for one logical ingestion

with the two ingestions one second apart, the second writer raised FileExistsError: immutable file differs: .../ingestion-69d43205265055ac.json, so the coordinator crashed out of ingestion rather than recognising a duplicate
three identical replays plus one regenerated retry produced INGESTED then three DUPLICATE_SUPPRESSED_BY_IDENTITY outcomes, leaving one ingestion file, one registry row and one PARENT_INGESTED event

why_this_is_a_defect: ingest_result derives its duplicate check from the SHA-256 of the entire callback document, so suppression only holds when the retry is byte-identical. The result document carries a perfectly good transaction identity — idempotency_key, lease_id, fence_token, attempt_id, result_commit_id and the artifact hashes — and none of it is used for suppression. A producer that re-emits after a lost callback therefore double-counts the unit, and two callbacks arriving together either double-count or crash the coordinator depending on the second on the clock.

metric_row_finding.detail: the deliverable asks for exactly one metric row per ingestion, but ingest_result writes none. metrics/work-unit-runs.jsonl is created empty at activation and was still empty (0 rows) after every fault class, so the append-only work-unit registry is the only per-ingestion durable effect that exists to be counted.
metric_row_finding.impact: duplicate metric rows are impossible today because metric rows are never written; the metric surface required by the metric-definitions contract is not populated at ingestion time

what_the_mechanism_does_hold: a byte-for-byte replay is genuinely harmless and is suppressed
no duplicate shape produced a false completion or a COMPLETED state
the hash-chained event file chain verified cleanly after every duplicate class
duplicate ingestion never fabricated an artifact: every accepted result still read back by immutable object id
no founder relay is involved in any part of the observed path

repair_candidate.approach: key suppression on the transaction identity the result already carries rather than on the message bytes, and claim that identity by exclusively creating a claim file before the live ingestion runs so a race collapses to exactly one effect
repair_candidate.adoption_authority: coordinator only; a subordinate producer may not modify workstreams/po03/tools/**

test_weakening_check: no assertion was relaxed to obtain a pass; the defect tests pin the observed double-count and the observed crash and will fail once suppression is keyed on the transaction identity
